windows.title: Unexpected restart (Kernel-Power 41)
windows.meaning: Windows started again without a clean shutdown first. The event only records that the previous session ended abruptly; it does not say why.
causes: Power loss or a held/pressed power button
System crash (bugcheck/blue screen) or a hard hang that was reset
Failing power supply, overheating or unstable overclock
Driver or firmware problems during sleep/hibernate
checks: Look for BugCheck 1001 and EventLog 6008 around the same time
Read BugcheckCode and PowerButtonTimestamp in the event data (0 = no bugcheck/no button press recorded)
Check power supply, UPS and temperatures if it repeats

windows.title: Entering sleep (Kernel-Power 42)
windows.meaning: The system is entering sleep; the event data gives the reason (e.g. user request, lid close, idle timeout).
causes: Sleep requested by the user or power plan
Lid closed or power button set to sleep
checks: If sleep is unwanted, review the power plan and the sleep reason

windows.title: Resumed from sleep (Kernel-Power 107)
windows.meaning: The system has resumed from sleep.
causes: Wake timer or wake-capable device (network adapter, mouse)
checks: If wakes are unwanted, run powercfg /lastwake and powercfg /waketimers

windows.title: Shutdown transition (Kernel-Power 109)
windows.meaning: The kernel power manager has initiated a shutdown transition. Logged on normal shutdowns and restarts, including Fast Startup.
causes: Shutdown or restart requested by a user, an installer or Windows Update
Power button configured to shut down
checks: See User32 1074 just before it for who or what requested the shutdown

windows.title: CPU speed limited by firmware (Kernel-Processor-Power 37)
windows.meaning: The processor speed is being limited by system firmware; the event says for how long since the last report.
causes: Power or battery limits set by the firmware
Power supply or docking station not delivering enough power
checks: Check temperatures, fans and dust
Check the power adapter and firmware/BIOS updates

windows.title: Operating system started (Kernel-General 12)
windows.meaning: Boot marker: records the time the operating system started.
checks: Use it to find restarts; check what happened just before it

windows.title: Operating system shutting down (Kernel-General 13)
windows.meaning: Records the time the operating system shut down cleanly.
checks: Its absence before a boot suggests an unclean shutdown

windows.title: Driver failed to load for a device (Kernel-PnP 219)
windows.meaning: A driver failed to load for a device during startup; the event names the driver and the device instance.
causes: Device not ready yet at boot (common for WudfRd and USB devices)
checks: Check the named device in Device Manager
Update or reinstall the driver if the device does not work

windows.title: Event log service started (EventLog 6005)
windows.meaning: Boot marker: the Event Log service started, which happens early on every boot.
checks: Use it to find restarts

windows.title: Event log service stopped (EventLog 6006)
windows.meaning: Shutdown marker: the Event Log service stopped during a clean shutdown.
checks: Its absence before a boot suggests an unclean shutdown

windows.title: Previous shutdown was unexpected (EventLog 6008)
windows.meaning: Logged at boot when the previous shutdown was not clean; it gives the time of the last known activity.
causes: Hard hang followed by a reset
checks: Look for Kernel-Power 41 and BugCheck 1001 at the same boot
Check what was logged just before the given time

windows.title: OS version at boot (EventLog 6009)
windows.meaning: Logged at boot with the Windows version and build.
checks: Compare builds across boots to spot upgrades

windows.title: System uptime (EventLog 6013)
windows.meaning: Daily record of the system uptime in seconds.
checks: A low value means a recent restart

windows.title: Security audit log cleared (1102)
windows.meaning: The Security log was cleared; the event names the account that did it.
checks: Confirm the named account and whether the clear was planned
Look for other suspicious activity around that time

windows.title: Event log cleared (Eventlog 104)
windows.meaning: An event log (such as System or Application) was cleared; the event names the log and the account.
causes: An administrator or script cleared the log
checks: Confirm the account and whether the clear was planned

windows.title: Planned shutdown or restart (User32 1074)
windows.meaning: A process initiated a restart or shutdown on behalf of a user; the event names the process, the user and the reason.
causes: Windows Update or an installer requested a restart
checks: Read the process, user and reason fields to see who or what restarted the device
windows.benignNote: Records a planned shutdown; useful to tell planned from unexpected restarts.

windows.title: Reason given for an unexpected shutdown (User32 1076)
windows.meaning: A user supplied a reason (Shutdown Event Tracker) for the last unexpected shutdown.
causes: Unexpected shutdown documented by an administrator
checks: Read the reason and comment; look for EventLog 6008 and Kernel-Power 41 around the original shutdown

windows.title: Restarted after a bugcheck / blue screen (BugCheck 1001)
windows.meaning: The computer restarted after a system crash (stop error). The event gives the stop code, its parameters and where the dump was saved.
causes: Hardware problems such as RAM, storage or overheating
checks: Look up the stop code (e.g. 0x0000009f, 0x00000124)
Analyze the dump in C:\Windows\Minidump or MEMORY.DMP
Check for recently updated drivers and WHEA-Logger errors

windows.title: Service failed to start (SCM 7000)
windows.meaning: A service failed to start; the event names the service and the error.
causes: Service is disabled or its account/password is wrong
checks: Check the service's start type, logon account and binary path
Look at the error text and related 7001/7009 events

windows.title: Service dependency failed (SCM 7001)
windows.meaning: A service did not start because a service it depends on failed to start.
causes: The named dependency failed (see its own 7000/7009/7023)
checks: Fix the dependency first; it is named in the event

windows.title: Service start timed out (SCM 7009)
windows.meaning: Windows waited too long (default 30 seconds) for a service to connect after starting it.
causes: Slow boot or high load (disk, CPU)
Service waits for network or another resource
checks: See whether 7000 follows for the same service
Check boot performance and disk health if many services time out

windows.title: Service did not respond in time (SCM 7011)
windows.meaning: A service did not answer a control request (such as stop or start) within the timeout.
causes: High system load or slow disk
checks: Check whether the service recovers; look for 7031/7034 for the same service

windows.title: Service hung on starting (SCM 7022)
windows.meaning: A service was started but did not report that it finished starting.
causes: Service waits for a resource or dependency
checks: Check the service's own logs and dependencies

windows.title: Service terminated with an error (SCM 7023)
windows.meaning: A service stopped and reported an error code; the event names the service and the error.
checks: Read the error text; check the service's configuration and logs

windows.title: Service terminated with a service-specific error (SCM 7024)
windows.meaning: A service stopped with an error code defined by the service itself.
checks: Look up the code in the vendor's documentation or the service's own log

windows.title: Boot or system driver failed to load (SCM 7026)
windows.meaning: One or more boot-start or system-start drivers failed to load; the event lists them.
checks: Identify the listed drivers; remove stale ones or update them

windows.title: Service crashed, recovery action taken (SCM 7031)
windows.meaning: A service terminated unexpectedly; the event says how many times it has done this and which recovery action will run.
checks: Look for Application Error 1000 / WER 1001 for the service's process
Check whether it repeats and update the software

windows.title: Service terminated unexpectedly (SCM 7034)
windows.meaning: A service terminated unexpectedly; no recovery action is configured.
checks: Look for Application Error 1000 for the same process
Consider configuring recovery actions

windows.title: Service state change (SCM 7036)
windows.meaning: A service entered the running or stopped state.
causes: Normal start/stop of services, many of which run on demand
checks: Only relevant when the timing matches a problem

windows.title: Service start type changed (SCM 7040)
windows.meaning: The start type of a service was changed (e.g. from automatic to manual); the event names the service and both types.
causes: Windows Update or BITS adjusting their own start type
checks: Check it if a security product or important service was set to disabled
windows.benignNote: Usually routine (often Background Intelligent Transfer Service); suspicious only for security services.

windows.title: New service installed (SCM 7045)
windows.meaning: A service was installed; the event names it, its image path, type, start type and account.
checks: Verify the image path and whether the installation was expected

windows.title: Application crash (Application Error 1000)
windows.meaning: An application crashed; the event names the program, the faulting module, the exception code and the offset.
causes: Bug in the application or a loaded module
Incompatible add-in, driver or security software
checks: Note the faulting module and exception code (0xc0000005 = access violation)
Update or repair the application
Check whether many different programs crash (points to system or hardware)

windows.title: Application hang (Application Hang 1002)
windows.meaning: A program stopped interacting with Windows and was closed.
causes: Program waiting on disk, network or a lock
checks: Check if it repeats for the same program and update it
Look for disk or network problems at the same time

windows.title: Problem report (Windows Error Reporting 1001)
windows.meaning: Windows Error Reporting recorded a problem report (fault bucket) with the event name (e.g. APPCRASH, BlueScreen, LiveKernelEvent) and the files attached.
causes: Usually follows another problem such as an application crash or hang
LiveKernelEvent reports driver or hardware recoveries without a crash
checks: Read the event name and parameters; match it with the related crash event

windows.title: Unhandled .NET exception (.NET Runtime 1026)
windows.meaning: A .NET application ended because of an unhandled exception; the event contains the exception type and stack trace.
checks: Read the exception type and stack; update or repair the application

windows.title: Bad block on disk (disk 7)
windows.meaning: The disk reported a bad block (unreadable sector).
checks: Check SMART status and back up data
Run chkdsk /scan and the vendor's disk diagnostics

windows.title: Disk controller error (disk 11)
windows.meaning: The driver detected a controller error on the named disk.
checks: Identify the disk number; check cables and SMART
Update storage controller drivers and firmware

windows.title: Error during paging operation (disk 51)
windows.meaning: An error was detected on a disk during a paging operation (reading or writing memory pages).
causes: Cable, controller or USB enclosure problems
checks: Check SMART and other disk errors for the same disk
Back up data if it repeats

windows.title: Disk I/O retried (disk 153)
windows.meaning: An I/O operation at a logical block address was retried on the named disk.
causes: Power management of the disk or link
checks: See whether it is frequent and combined with disk 7/51 or storport 129
Check SMART, firmware and controller drivers

windows.title: Disk surprise removed (disk 157)
windows.meaning: A disk was removed without warning.
causes: Disk dropped off the bus because of power or hardware problems
checks: Check whether it was a removable disk; if internal, check power, cables and disk health

windows.title: Storage reset issued (storport 129)
windows.meaning: The storage driver issued a reset to a device because a request did not complete in time.
causes: Disk or SSD not responding (firmware, failing drive)
checks: Update SSD firmware and storage drivers
Check SMART and whether disk 153 events appear at the same time

windows.title: NVMe controller error (stornvme 11)
windows.meaning: The NVMe driver detected a controller error on the named port.
checks: Check drive temperature, SMART and firmware updates

windows.title: File system corruption (Ntfs 55)
windows.meaning: NTFS detected corruption in the file system structure of a volume.
checks: Run chkdsk on the volume (schedule /f or use /scan)
Check disk health

windows.title: Volume health status (Ntfs 98)
windows.meaning: NTFS reports the health of a volume when it is mounted. 'Is healthy' means no action is needed; otherwise it asks for a check.
causes: Volume mounted at boot or when a drive is attached
checks: Read the text: act only if it says the volume needs a check or repair
windows.benignNote: Harmless when the message says the volume is healthy.

windows.title: File system repaired (Ntfs 130)
windows.meaning: The file system structure on a volume has been repaired.
causes: Earlier corruption fixed by self-healing or chkdsk
checks: Look for the cause of the corruption (disk errors, unclean shutdowns)

windows.title: Transaction resource manager error (Ntfs 137)
windows.meaning: The default transaction resource manager of a volume hit an error (its transaction metadata may have been reset).
causes: File system problems on the volume
checks: Check for other NTFS or disk errors on the same volume; run chkdsk /scan if any

windows.title: Crash dump initialization failed (volmgr 46)
windows.meaning: Windows could not set up crash dump writing at boot, so a crash may not leave a dump file.
causes: No or too small paging file on the boot volume
Crash dump settings or storage driver issues
checks: Check the page file and the Startup and Recovery dump settings

windows.title: Dump file creation failed (volmgr 161)
windows.meaning: Writing the crash dump failed during a system crash.
causes: Paging file too small or missing
checks: Check page file size and dump settings
Look at the BugCheck event of that boot

windows.title: Hardware error reported (WHEA-Logger 1)
windows.meaning: Windows Hardware Error Architecture reported a hardware error; the text says whether it was corrected or fatal and which component reported it.
causes: CPU, memory, PCIe or bus errors
checks: Read the component and error source in the message
Check BIOS/firmware updates and hardware diagnostics

windows.title: Corrected hardware error (WHEA-Logger 17)
windows.meaning: A corrected hardware error occurred, typically reported by a PCI Express component; the system kept running.
causes: PCIe link errors (often with link power management)
checks: Identify the device from the bus/device/function in the event
Update chipset drivers and BIOS; reseat the device if it repeats

windows.title: Fatal hardware error (WHEA-Logger 18)
windows.meaning: A fatal hardware error occurred (machine check); it usually caused a crash and restart.
checks: Remove overclocks, check temperatures and power
Update BIOS; run memory and CPU diagnostics

windows.title: Corrected machine check (WHEA-Logger 19)
windows.meaning: A corrected hardware error was reported by the processor (cache, bus or interconnect).
checks: Check frequency of occurrence; update BIOS/microcode
Remove overclocks

windows.title: Corrected memory error (WHEA-Logger 47)
windows.meaning: A corrected memory error (e.g. ECC) occurred.
checks: Watch the rate; run memory diagnostics
Replace the module if errors increase

windows.title: Successful logon (4624)
windows.meaning: An account logged on successfully; the logon type tells how (2 interactive, 3 network, 5 service, 7 unlock, 10 remote desktop, 11 cached).
causes: Normal user, service or network logons
checks: Look at the account, logon type and source address for unusual access
windows.benignNote: Very frequent; relevant only for unexpected accounts or sources.

windows.title: Failed logon (4625)
windows.meaning: A logon attempt failed; Status/Sub Status give the reason (0xC000006A wrong password, 0xC0000064 unknown user, 0xC0000234 account locked, 0xC0000072 disabled).
causes: Mistyped password or stale saved credentials
Service or task with an old password
checks: Group by account, source address and logon type
Many failures from one address suggest brute force

windows.title: Logoff (4634)
windows.meaning: A logon session ended.
causes: Normal logoff or network session ending
checks: Pair with 4624 by Logon ID if session duration matters

windows.title: Logon with explicit credentials (4648)
windows.meaning: A process tried to log on using explicitly supplied credentials (for example runas or mapping a drive with another account).
causes: Scheduled tasks or scripts using stored credentials
checks: Check the process and target account for anything unexpected

windows.title: Special privileges assigned (4672)
windows.meaning: A new logon was given sensitive privileges (administrator-equivalent).
checks: Unexpected accounts here deserve a look

windows.title: User account created (4720)
windows.meaning: A user account was created; the event names the new account and who created it.
checks: Verify the account was expected

windows.title: User account enabled (4722)
windows.meaning: A user account was enabled.
checks: Verify it was expected, especially for built-in accounts

windows.title: User account disabled (4725)
windows.meaning: A user account was disabled.
checks: Verify it was expected

windows.title: User account deleted (4726)
windows.meaning: A user account was deleted.
checks: Verify it was expected

windows.title: Member added to a local group (4732)
windows.meaning: A member was added to a security-enabled local group (for example Administrators or Remote Desktop Users).
checks: Check the group and the added member, especially for Administrators

windows.title: Account locked out (4740)
windows.meaning: A user account was locked out after too many failed logons; the event names the caller computer.
causes: Stale password on a phone, mapped drive, service or task
checks: Find the source in Caller Computer Name and the 4625/4771/4776 events before it

windows.title: Account unlocked (4767)
windows.meaning: A user account was unlocked.
checks: Correlate with the earlier lockout (4740)

windows.title: Kerberos pre-authentication failed (4771)
windows.meaning: Kerberos pre-authentication failed (logged on domain controllers); failure code 0x18 usually means a wrong password.
checks: Check the client address and failure code

windows.title: NTLM credential validation (4776)
windows.meaning: The computer attempted to validate credentials for an account using NTLM; a non-zero error code means it failed (0xC000006A wrong password, 0xC0000064 unknown user).
checks: Check the error code and the source workstation

windows.title: DCOM permission (DistributedCOM 10016)
windows.meaning: A component tried to start or activate a COM server without the configured local launch/activation permission.
causes: Windows components behaving as designed; Microsoft documents these as expected
checks: Ignore unless a specific feature is failing at the same time
windows.benignNote: Microsoft documents 10016 as expected noise that does not affect functionality.

windows.title: COM server did not register in time (DistributedCOM 10010)
windows.meaning: A COM server (named by CLSID) did not register with DCOM within the required timeout.
causes: Component slow to start or failing
High load at logon or boot
checks: Identify the CLSID; act only if a related feature fails

windows.title: TLS fatal alert received (Schannel 36887)
windows.meaning: The remote side ended a TLS handshake with a fatal alert; the alert code tells why (e.g. 40 handshake failure, 42/46 certificate problem, 48 unknown CA, 70 protocol version).
causes: Certificate not trusted by the remote side
checks: Only investigate if a specific connection or application is failing

windows.title: TLS fatal alert sent (Schannel 36888)
windows.meaning: This computer ended a TLS handshake with a fatal alert; the alert code and internal error state tell why.
causes: Remote side offers unsupported protocols or ciphers
checks: Investigate only if a service on this device has TLS problems

windows.title: No common TLS cipher suite (Schannel 36874)
windows.meaning: A client connected but none of its cipher suites is supported by this server.
causes: Old client or scanner using outdated ciphers
Server hardened beyond what a client supports
checks: Identify the client if a legitimate application fails

windows.title: DNS name resolution timed out (DNS Client 1014)
windows.meaning: Name resolution for a name timed out because none of the configured DNS servers responded.
causes: Network not ready yet (boot, resume, VPN changes)
checks: Check whether it happens only at boot/resume or continuously
Verify DNS server settings if many different names fail
windows.benignNote: Often harmless, especially for wpad or right after boot/resume.

windows.title: No domain time source (Time-Service 129)
windows.meaning: NtpClient could not find a domain controller to use as a time source and will retry.
causes: No connection to the domain (off-site, VPN not up)
checks: Check domain connectivity; run w32tm /query /status

windows.title: Manual time peer not resolvable (Time-Service 134)
windows.meaning: NtpClient could not use the configured manual time server because of a DNS resolution error and will retry.
causes: No network or DNS at that moment
Time server name wrong or blocked
checks: Check whether the time later synchronizes (w32tm /query /status)
windows.benignNote: Common right after boot or when the device is offline.

windows.title: Time not synchronized (Time-Service 36)
windows.meaning: The time service has not synchronized the system time for a long period because no time source provided a usable time stamp.
checks: Run w32tm /query /status and w32tm /resync
Check UDP 123 to the configured source

windows.title: Update installed (WindowsUpdateClient 19)
windows.meaning: Windows Update installed an update successfully; the event names it.
checks: Useful to correlate problems that started after an update

windows.title: Update installation failed (WindowsUpdateClient 20)
windows.meaning: Windows Update failed to install an update; the event names it and the error code.
causes: Damaged component store or update cache
checks: Look up the error code
Check free space; run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth and sfc /scannow

windows.title: Update installation started (WindowsUpdateClient 43)
windows.meaning: Windows Update started installing an update.
checks: Pair with 19 (success) or 20 (failure)

windows.title: Update download started (WindowsUpdateClient 44)
windows.meaning: Windows Update started downloading an update.
checks: None unless downloads never complete

windows.title: Group Policy: no domain controller (GroupPolicy 1129)
windows.meaning: Group Policy processing failed because there was no network connectivity to a domain controller.
causes: Device off-site or VPN not connected
checks: Check whether later processing succeeds; check DNS and domain connectivity

windows.title: Group Policy: could not resolve user/computer (GroupPolicy 1053)
windows.meaning: Group Policy processing failed because Windows could not resolve the user or computer name.
checks: Run gpupdate /force and check the error details
Test the secure channel and DNS

windows.title: Group Policy extension failed (GroupPolicy 1085)
windows.meaning: Windows failed to apply the settings of one Group Policy extension (named in the event).
causes: Invalid or unreachable policy item (e.g. a file path or printer)
checks: Run gpresult /h report.html and check the named extension

windows.title: No secure session with a domain controller (NETLOGON 5719)
windows.meaning: The computer could not set up a secure session with a domain controller.
checks: If only at boot and logons work, it is usually transient
Otherwise test with nltest /sc_query:<domain>

windows.title: Could not authenticate with a domain controller (NETLOGON 3210)
windows.meaning: The computer could not authenticate with a domain controller, so domain logons may fail.
causes: Machine account password out of sync (restored image or snapshot)
checks: Test-ComputerSecureChannel; repair or rejoin the domain if broken

windows.title: IP address conflict (Tcpip 4199)
windows.meaning: The system detected another device using the same IP address; the event names the address and the other MAC address.
causes: Static address overlapping the DHCP range
Two devices configured with the same address
checks: Find the device with the given MAC address; fix the address assignment

windows.title: User logon notification (Winlogon 7001)
windows.meaning: Winlogon recorded a user logon (Customer Experience Improvement Program notification).
checks: Use it to see when users logged on

windows.title: User logoff notification (Winlogon 7002)
windows.meaning: Winlogon recorded a user logoff.
checks: Use it to see when users logged off

windows.title: Boot performance (Diagnostics-Performance 100)
windows.meaning: Windows recorded how long startup took (boot duration and main/post-boot phases).
checks: Compare boot durations over time; look at 101-110 events for slow components
windows.benignNote: Informational; long durations point to slow startup.

windows.title: Shutdown performance (Diagnostics-Performance 200)
windows.meaning: Windows recorded how long shutdown took.
checks: Look at 201-206 events for components that slowed shutdown

windows.title: Database log file error (ESENT 455)
windows.meaning: A component using the ESE database engine could not open a log file; the event names the process, the file and the error.
causes: Missing folder or file (often error -1811 for a missing log directory)
Damaged database files of a Windows component
checks: Identify the process and path; act only if that component misbehaves

windows.title: Database file access denied (ESENT 490)
windows.meaning: A component using the ESE database engine could not open a file for read/write access.
causes: File locked by another program such as antivirus
checks: Identify the process and file; check whether the component works

windows.title: Volume Shadow Copy error (VSS 8193)
windows.meaning: The Volume Shadow Copy Service hit an unexpected error calling a routine; the event shows the routine and HRESULT.
causes: Backup or restore point software issues
checks: Run vssadmin list writers to check writer states
Check whether backups and restore points work

windows.title: Volume Shadow Copy device error (VSS 12289)
windows.meaning: The Volume Shadow Copy Service got an unexpected error from a device I/O control call on a volume.
causes: Volume does not support shadow copies (e.g. some removable or virtual volumes)
checks: Check which volume is named and whether backups of it fail

windows.title: Volume Shadow Copy COM server problem (VSS 13)
windows.meaning: Volume Shadow Copy Service information: a COM server it needs could not be started or used.
checks: Check vssadmin list writers and whether backups succeed

windows.title: Network link disconnected (Intel Ethernet 27)
windows.meaning: The Intel Ethernet adapter reported that the network link is disconnected.
causes: Power management turning the adapter off
checks: Check how often it repeats; check cable and switch port
Update the network driver; review power management settings

linux.pattern: Out of memory: Kill(?:ed)? process|oom-kill:|invoked oom-killer|Memory cgroup out of memory
linux.title: Out of memory (OOM killer)
linux.meaning: The kernel ran out of memory and killed a process to free it; the message names the process and its memory use.
causes: A process using too much memory (leak or load)
Too little RAM or swap for the workload
checks: Identify the killed process and its memory use
Check free -m, swap and service memory limits

linux.title: Killed by systemd-oomd
linux.meaning: systemd-oomd killed a unit or process because of memory pressure.
checks: Check which unit was killed and its memory use (systemd-cgtop)

linux.title: Process crashed (segfault)
linux.meaning: A process crashed with an invalid memory access; the kernel logs the program, address and library involved.
causes: Bug in the program or a library
Incompatible library versions after an update
checks: Check coredumpctl list for a core dump
Update the program; run a memory test if crashes are widespread

linux.pattern: I/O error, dev \w+|blk_update_request: (?:I/O|critical medium|critical target) error|Buffer I/O error on dev
linux.title: Disk I/O error
linux.meaning: The kernel reported a failed read or write on a block device; the message names the device and sector.
causes: Cable, controller or USB enclosure problems
checks: Run smartctl -a on the device
Check dmesg for resets or link errors on the same device
Back up data if errors repeat

linux.title: ext4 file system error
linux.meaning: ext4 detected an inconsistency or I/O problem on the file system; it may be remounted read-only.
checks: Check disk health (smartctl)
Run fsck on the file system while it is unmounted

linux.title: XFS corruption detected
linux.meaning: XFS detected metadata corruption; it may shut down the file system to prevent damage.
checks: Check disk health
Run xfs_repair on the unmounted file system (after a backup)

linux.pattern: Failed with result '|entered failed state|Main process exited, code=(?:exited|killed|dumped)|Failed to start
linux.title: systemd unit failed
linux.meaning: A systemd service stopped with an error or did not start; the result (e.g. exit-code, signal, timeout, core-dump) tells how.
checks: Run systemctl status <unit> and journalctl -u <unit> -b
Check the service's configuration

linux.pattern: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup|BUG: soft lockup|watchdog: Watchdog detected hard LOCKUP|rcu_(?:sched|preempt) (?:self-)?detected stall
linux.title: CPU lockup / stall
linux.meaning: A CPU was stuck in kernel code for too long; the system may hang.
checks: Note the module/function in the stack trace
Update the kernel and drivers; check the hypervisor if it is a VM

linux.title: Task hung
linux.meaning: A process was blocked in the kernel (usually waiting for I/O) for longer than the hung-task timeout.
checks: Look for disk or NFS errors at the same time
Check I/O load with iostat

linux.pattern: \[Hardware Error\]|mce: |Machine check events logged|Machine Check Exception
linux.title: Hardware error (machine check)
linux.meaning: The CPU reported a machine check: a hardware error, corrected or not, in the CPU, memory or bus.
checks: Check rasdaemon/mcelog output if installed
Run memory diagnostics; check temperatures and firmware

linux.pattern: Failed password for|Invalid user \S+ from|Failed publickey for
linux.title: Failed SSH login
linux.meaning: An SSH login attempt failed (wrong password or unknown user); the message gives the user and source address.
causes: Automated password guessing from the internet
checks: Count attempts per source address
Consider key-only authentication, fail2ban or firewall rules

linux.title: Authentication failure (PAM)
linux.meaning: PAM reported a failed authentication for a service such as sshd, sudo or login.
checks: Check the service, user and rhost fields; look for repeats

linux.title: Kernel panic
linux.meaning: The kernel hit a fatal error and stopped; the reason follows 'not syncing'.
causes: Missing or damaged root file system or initramfs
checks: Read the panic reason and previous messages
Check for kdump/pstore data; update the kernel

linux.pattern: nvme\S*:.*(?:timeout|I/O \d+ QID \d+ timeout|controller is down|Removing after probe failure)
linux.title: NVMe timeout or controller reset
linux.meaning: An NVMe drive did not answer in time and the driver aborted or reset it.
checks: Check smartctl -a and nvme smart-log
Update SSD firmware; consider nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us=0 if APST is suspected

linux.pattern: Link is Down|link is not ready|NIC Link is Down|carrier lost
linux.title: Network link down
linux.meaning: A network interface lost its link (cable/carrier) or is not ready yet.
checks: Check whether it recovers (Link is Up) and how often it repeats
Check cable, switch port and driver

linux.title: CPU overheating or throttling
linux.meaning: The CPU got too hot and was throttled; at critical temperatures the system shuts down.
checks: Check sensors output and fans
Clean the cooling system; check the workload

linux.pattern: corrupted or uncleanly shut down, renaming and replacing|systemd-journald.*corrupt
linux.title: Journal file corrupted or not closed
linux.meaning: journald found a journal file that was not closed cleanly or is damaged and replaced it.
checks: Check for an unclean shutdown before it; check disk health if it repeats
linux.benignNote: Usually harmless after an unclean shutdown; journald recovers automatically.

macos.pattern: userspace watchdog timeout|watchdog timeout: no successful checkins|WatchdogTimeout
macos.title: Watchdog timeout (macOS)
macos.meaning: A watchdog found that an essential system process (often WindowServer) stopped checking in, and macOS forced a panic and restart.
causes: A hung system process, often graphics / WindowServer
A faulty driver or kernel extension
checks: Read which process stopped checking in (in the panic report)
Look for GPU, display or storage errors before it
Install pending macOS updates

macos.title: Kernel panic (macOS)
macos.meaning: macOS stopped at the kernel level and restarted. The panic report gives the panic string and the kernel extensions in the backtrace.
causes: A faulty or incompatible kernel extension or driver
A system process that stopped responding (watchdog)
checks: Read the panic string and the extensions in the backtrace of the report
Check whether it repeats; disconnect peripherals and remove third-party extensions
Run Apple Diagnostics and install pending macOS updates

macos.title: Application crash report (macOS)
macos.meaning: A process crashed and macOS wrote a crash report with the exception type, the crashed thread and a backtrace.
causes: A bug in the app or a plugin it loaded
An app version that does not fit the macOS version
Memory or disk problems (when many apps crash)
checks: Read Exception Type and the top frames of the crashed thread
Update or reinstall the app; check whether it repeats
If many apps crash, check memory and disk health

macos.title: Process ended because of memory pressure (macOS)
macos.meaning: macOS ended a process to free memory (memorystatus / jetsam), or because swap space ran low.
causes: Too little memory for the workload
Low free space on the startup disk (swap files live there)
checks: See which process was ended and how much memory it used
Check free space on the startup disk
Watch memory pressure in Activity Monitor

macos.title: Sleep/wake failure (macOS)
macos.meaning: The Mac did not sleep or wake correctly; it is often followed by a restart.
causes: A driver or peripheral that fails during sleep
checks: Run pmset -g log and read the entries around that time
Disconnect peripherals and install pending macOS updates

macos.pattern: Failed password for|Invalid user \S+ from|Failed publickey for|authentication error for
macos.title: Failed SSH login (macOS)
macos.meaning: An SSH login (Remote Login) failed: a wrong password, an unknown user name or a rejected key.
causes: A wrong key configured on the client
checks: Look at the source address and how often it repeats
If Remote Login need not be reachable, turn it off or restrict it

macos.pattern: authentication fail|failed to authenticate|authentication error|incorrect password
macos.title: Authentication failure (macOS)
macos.meaning: A login, sudo, screen unlock, screen sharing or authorization request was refused.
causes: A wrong or changed password (also network accounts)
Repeated attempts by a script or an attacker
checks: See which process and user it was (loginwindow, sudo, sshd, screensharingd)
Check how often it repeats and from where

macos.title: Installation or update failed (macOS)
macos.meaning: Installing a package, an app or a macOS update did not complete.
causes: A damaged or blocked package (signature, MDM or security policy)
checks: Run softwareupdate --history and check free disk space
Read /var/log/install.log around that time

macos.title: Disk or APFS error (macOS)
macos.meaning: The storage reported an I/O error, or APFS found damaged file system data.
causes: A failing drive, cable or enclosure (external disks)
File system damage after a power loss
checks: Run First Aid in Disk Utility (diskutil verifyVolume)
Check the drive's SMART status (diskutil info disk0) and the backups
